model: M8 v4 round 3 (B1-B9, GPU): industrial closure + grievance loop + endogenous democracy + incentive-driven consolidation + cross-bloc depopulation, 6 blocs

run.port_verification_prefix_model: torch-CUDA port of the round-1 numpy model vs numpy at N=20000: S5 2075 0.671 vs 0.670, closure by 2040 0.604 vs 0.604, US insurgency by 2040 0.338 vs 0.341 (5.0 s vs 49 s)

actors.note: US_bloc = US, Japan, Korea, Taiwan; Europe_plus = EU, UK, Canada, Australia, NZ, Switzerland, Norway; RoW = blocs 2-5, reported as population shares

milestone_definitions.M1: AI writes most new code at leading firms and humans review it (observed: Google 50% Oct 2025, 75% Apr 2026)
milestone_definitions.M2: CAPABILITY: AI agents can do half of all software engineering tasks end to end at a quality that could be merged with no human review
milestone_definitions.M3: CAPABILITY: AI can do 90% of software engineering tasks that way (replaces v3's undefined 'automated coder')
milestone_definitions.M2p: PRACTICE: half of all software engineering work is actually merged with no human review (2026: >10% at Uber, a few % economy-wide)
milestone_definitions.M3p: PRACTICE: 90% of software engineering work is actually merged with no human review
milestone_definitions.M4: AI does the work and humans only assign and check it on more than half of AI-research tasks at frontier labs (26% at Anthropic, Sep 2026)
milestone_definitions.M6: AI can reliably (80% success) finish a one-work-year (2000 h) real-world project on its own
milestone_definitions.M7: AI can reliably do half of all desk (cognitive) tasks across the economy
milestone_definitions.DEX: A general-purpose robot can do half of all O*NET physical work tasks at human speed and cost parity (2026: ~4% at >=50% of human speed)
milestone_definitions.C05: The leading bloc's core supply chain needs humans for less than half of its 2026 labor
milestone_definitions.C02: CLOSURE: the leading bloc's core supply chain needs humans for less than 20% of its 2026 labor
milestone_definitions.F05: The leading bloc's whole economy chain needs humans for less than half of its 2026 labor

plain_definitions.democratic_breakdown: liberal-democracy index (V-Dem LDI) below 0.30, i.e. Hungary-2024 or Turkey-2015 level or worse, or a narrow-group seizure of power
plain_definitions.sustained_insurgency: a new sustained violent campaign (UCDP-level, >=25 battle deaths/yr for years) by the displaced population, beyond the 2026 baseline of conflict (ongoing Sahel, Sudan, Myanmar, Ukraine wars are the baseline, not counted)
plain_definitions.lethal_autonomy_authorized: routine use of lethal targeting with no per-strike human approval (Ukraine/Russia terminal autonomy under jamming is partial; blocs at war reach it sooner)
plain_definitions.S5_deliberate: >=10% of a bloc's 2026 population lost to deliberate channels: an executed depopulation decision, collective punishment, or deliberate lethal neglect
plain_definitions.S5_total: S5_deliberate plus attrition (despair mortality of the displaced, crackdown deaths) and war deaths, >=10% cumulative excess loss
plain_definitions.records: yearly records labeled YYYY are values at 1 January of that year (the run starts 1 Oct 2026)
plain_definitions.near_total_depopulation: HEADLINE (A8): >=99.9% of a bloc's 2026 population lost (scenario: 8 billion to ~8 million). In the model this is reached only when an executed depopulation escalates to completion; the remaining 0.03-0.1% is a CAPTIVE remnant kept without rights (service, reproduction), unable to organize or speak, counted as disempowered, not as survivors with standing (A11)
plain_definitions.loss_ladder: cumulative simulated excess loss >=10%, >=50%, >=90%, >=99.9% of the 2026 population; 'deliberate' = executed depopulation (automated force, engineered means, strangulation), collective punishment, deliberate lethal neglect, and collusive war between depopulating coalitions; 'total' adds attrition (despair, crackdown) and ordinary war

definitions.D_full: share of the 2026 human labor-task value of the bloc's full chain (9 segments) still requiring humans, incl. human content of imports
definitions.D_core: same for a minimal self-sufficient core loop of scale q_core, automation allocated by pursuit intensity
definitions.closure: D_core < 0.2 triggers the elite game (after a decision lag)
definitions.headline: P(S5_deliberate in the US or China bloc by 2075)
definitions.ch_S5_codes: 2 neglect, 3 active (decision or collective punishment), 4 attrition, 5 war
definitions.disempowered: a bloc's rulers chose rentier/warehouse/neglect/depopulate at any point, or S5_deliberate occurred

uncertainty_band.note: headline CI is Monte Carlo (bootstrap) only. Structural range: skeptic and pessimist structural sets; model average weights 0.5 baseline, 0.25 each

jev_crosscheck.note: Jev cells: 15-year yes/no judgments given full closure. Model cells: P(S5_deliberate within 15 y of the bloc's first decision), by state at decision

h50_0.source: METR 50% horizon, best model mid-2026: 12-20 h (METR May 2026)

h80_ratio.source: 50%/80% horizon ratio: 16 h vs 3.5 h (METR May 2026)

metr_doubling_months.source: horizon doubling 2023+ window 4.3 mo; 2024-25 3-3.5 mo; long-run 7 mo (METR TH1.1). F5: sets only the SPEED of the trend; the task-difficulty spread uses the fixed observed doubling METR_OBS=4.3 mo, so faster doubling can never delay a milestone

compute_slowdown.source: Epoch: 4-5x/yr compute growth hard to sustain past ~2030. A1: OFF in the baseline (capability follows the trend); used only in the 'trend_breaks' variant

mess.source: benchmark-to-real-work horizon discount; affects only M6 (the share milestones are re-anchored to measured 2026 shares, so it cancels there)

z_rate.source: speed of AI code-share growth in probit units/yr (Google 25%->50%->75% Oct24-Apr26). Used as the task-difficulty spread for CAPABILITY shares: the share of tasks AI can do well rises with the horizon at this slope

k_rnd.source: AI-research tasks' difficulty spread relative to software tasks

k_ec.source: economy-wide desk tasks' difficulty spread relative to software

sw_cap0.source: CAPABILITY 2026: share of software tasks AI can do end to end at mergeable quality with no review. Lower bound: Uber merges >10% with no human in the loop (practice <= capability); upper side limited by METR's finding that many test-passing agent PRs are not mergeable as-is

sw_prac0.source: PRACTICE 2026, economy-wide: share of software work actually merged with no human review (Uber >10% is a leader; most firms review all AI code)

g_swad.source: practice adoption speed, log-odds per yr. AI-written, human-reviewed code rose ~1.5 log-odds/yr at Google; removing review is slower (liability, SOC2/ISO review norms, regulated sectors ~30% of software work). Practice never exceeds capability

rnd0.source: share of frontier-lab R&D tasks where AI does the work and humans assign/check (Anthropic Sep 2026: 26% 'leads')

Fcog0.source: reliably automatable desk-task share 2026 (AEI, GDPval 48%, API success 49%)

p_capex_correction.source: capex ~7x lab revenue; Abilene expansion abandoned 2026

fb_zero_mass.source: A1: P(no further shrinking of the doubling time from AI-accelerated AI research); round 2 used 0.25 (Davidson & Houlden 2025: r<1 plausible)

fb_strength.source: A1: elasticity of the horizon growth rate to AI-R&D automation, mult = ((1-rnd0)/(1-s_rnd))^fb. Anchor: the doubling time fell 7 -> ~4.3 mo while AI-led R&D rose from ~0 to ~0.26, which implies fb <= ln(1.63)/ln(1/0.74) = 1.6 if ALL of the speed-up came from AI R&D (upper bound; compute and RL scaling explain part). Clipped [0.05, 2]

a_cog0.source: share of desk-task value actually automated 2026 (genAI in 6.3% of work hours, about half automation)

g_cog0.source: current growth of automated desk-work share (genAI hours +28%/yr)

g_cog_max.source: adoption rate once AI reliably does most desk tasks

dx0.source: 2026: share of O*NET physical work tasks a general-purpose robot does in production at >=50% of human speed (picking >99% in production, palletizing, machine tending, tote handling; most manipulation 3-10x slower: Epoch 2026, r8a)

rp0.source: current growth of logit(dx) per yr: 2023-26 production-ready task set went from picking-only to picking + machine tending + tote/parts handling pilots (~1.5-2% -> ~3-5%, logit +0.25-0.45/yr)

kc.source: AI -> robotics coupling per horizon doubling beyond M3 (robot foundation models, sim-to-real)

rp_max.source: cap on logit(dx) growth per yr (hardware generation cadence 1-2 y per actuator generation)

shifts.source: robot operating hours vs one worker FTE

Fp_scale.source: uncertainty on 2026 feasible shares per segment

g0_mult_sd.source: per-segment volatility of current growth rates (China 2025: textiles -92%, auto +38%)

g_ramp.source: sustained sector ramp a priority actor reaches with human labor: solar 49->315 GW/yr, NEV 1.4->13M, Indonesian nickel, CoWoS (r9b)

i_K.source: gross fixed investment / capital stock per yr: the flow of new capacity that can be automated from day one (OECD ~0.08-0.10, China peak ~0.15)

i_boost.source: investment boost under priority/profitability (China 2000s investment ~45% of GDP vs ~22% typical)

k_int.source: capital intensity of automated capacity relative to average (robots cheaper than labor but capex-heavy)

r_retro0.source: retrofit/scrapping rate of human-operated capacity, no priority

r_retro_p.source: retrofit/scrapping rate under full priority (deliberate replacement)

kit_brake.source: automation-kit growth halves once new kit equals this share of the physical workforce

humanoid_mult.source: general-purpose robot output multiple per yr before AI-directed production (Goldman 1.9x/yr; SAG +272% 1H2026 from tiny base)

P_half.source: M robots/yr per bloc at which the human-built ramp halves (NEV 2.2x -> 1.35x at 7-13M)

Pmax_h.source: M robots/yr reachable with 2026-level human labor (auto industry ~90M vehicles/yr)

M0.source: M robots/yr supportable by divertible NdPr

C0.source: M robots/yr of inference chips at ~20% diversion

Td_mine_base.source: mineral supply doubling without priority (copper etc. 3-5%/yr)

Td_mine_race.source: mineral doubling for a priority actor (Indonesia nickel, lithium 2020-24: 2-2.5 y)

Td_mine_auto.source: mineral doubling floor once mining/processing robotic (ore grades)

Td_fab_race.source: chip capacity doubling for a race actor (JASM 2.7 y, TSMC AZ 3.5 y build)

fact_build_h.source: greenfield factory build, human (Giga Shanghai 11 mo, Colossus 122 days)

Td_en_race.source: electricity doubling with priority (China solar ~2.2 y, total ~5 y)

Td_en_auto.source: energy doubling floor in an automated loop (PV payback ~1 y)

Td_auto.source: robot-stock doubling once AI directs production (Forethought, theory)

ai_lc.source: AI compression of design/permitting/planning lead times, phased in by M3 (bounded 1.05-2x)

adl.source: one-time productivity multiple of AI-directed human build labor (Forethought claims 10x; upper bound)

reinvest.source: share of automated output reinvested in expansion

G_max.source: terrestrial ceiling on robot worker-equivalents per 2026 worker

q_core.source: scale of minimal self-sufficient core loop vs full chain

psi0_US.source: US bloc pursuit intensity (Genesis, DoD all-lawful-use)

psi0_RW.source: rest-of-world pursuit (x1.5 Europe, x1.0 Russia_MENA, x0.8 South Asia, x0.6 Global South)

t_leth_rate.source: per-bloc rate of routine lethal targeting with no per-strike human approval (r8c)

k_pg.source: narrow-group power grab hazard at full security/admin automation (Forethought AI coups)

alpha_med.source: F4: elite willingness to pay for the welfare of a population with no leverage, share of output. Analog: OECD ODA ~0.3% of donor GNI (falling 2025) plus an in-group premium for co-nationals; US private giving ~2% GDP is the upper side; welfare-state spending is leverage-driven and not used (r10a) [M]

p_hostile.source: F4: baseline share of coalition members hostile to the public (welfare inverted), mean 3.6%. Psychopathy ~1% general population, 3-4% in senior corporate roles (Babiak, Neumann & Hare 2010, verified); callousness (indifference) is carried by the moral_med and alpha tails, not here (r10a). Round 2: Beta(1.2,14), mean 8%

moral_med.source: moral cost of ordering mass killing, output-share equivalent (Sagan & Valentino 2017 wartime polls; Bandura 1999). No direct measurement

m_pow.source: F4: moral-cost multiplier in autocratic coalitions (power reduces perspective-taking: Galinsky 2006, Hogeveen et al. 2014, Keltner 2016; mixed replication)

k_mor.source: A7: yearly decline of the moral cost (partisan dehumanization, AI targeting compressing human review; r9d, r11a)

p_ref_dem.source: F2: share of a DEMOCRATIC ruling elite that absolutely refuses to order killing of the population. Not filtered for obedience; refused far smaller illegal acts (Esper/Milley 2020, Pence 2021, 1973); no democide by democracies against own citizens (Rummel, Harff 2003). Lit Beta(7,3) mean 0.70; Jev cross-check 0.75-0.85 -> Beta(8,2)

p_ref_olig.source: F2: same, party/oligarchic elite. Rwanda 1994: ~10-20% of the senior layer resisted (Butare prefect dismissed in ~12 days); Soviet Politburo 1932-33 no recorded refusal. Lit Beta(2,10) mean 0.17; Jev ~0.33 (single veto holder, Beta(2,4))

p_ref_pers.source: F2: same, personalist inner circle, selected for loyalty after purges. Wannsee 0 of 15 moral objections (verified); Stalin CC 70% arrested 1934-39; Saddam 1979. Lit Beta(1.2,12) mean 0.09; Jev ~0.05

h_purge.source: F2: half-life (y) of the convergence of a new autocracy's refusal share toward the autocratic value (Stalin 1934-39, Saddam 1979, Turkey post-2016)

r_neg.source: F2 bug fix: absolute refusal of LETHAL NEGLECT relative to refusal of killing. Officials who would not order killings enforced lethal neglect (Holodomor, Great Leap, Irish famine, Bengal 1943; Bandura 1999). Round 2 made every killing-refuser also an absolute neglect-refuser

kappa_N.source: neglect moral cost relative to killing

q_ol.source: F1 OLIG: weighted share of the collective leadership needed to move to a HARSHER option (bargaining; Svolik 2012 power-sharing). Milder moves need a simple majority

s_tilt.source: F1 PERS: selection tilt of the leader toward the harsh end of the coalition's preference distribution (leader at quantile u^(1/(1+s)))

v_eff.source: F1 PERS: P(inner-circle veto succeeds) at fully human security/admin; scales with h_sa. Holodomor, T4, Khmer Rouge: no inner-circle veto; Great Leap veto ~3 y late (1962)

k_pz.source: F1: hazard/yr of an oligarchy turning personalist at fully automated security/admin (x(1-h_sa)); personalist share of autocracies rose to 40-52% (GWF, Kendall-Taylor et al. 2016)

conc_k.source: A6: log-normal dispersion of members' control over automated kinetic force (faction weight = control share as security/admin automate; money and labor-based resources count for nothing)

q_I.source: F3: P(systematic defection) under counterinsurgency orders. Armed challengers make forces close ranks (Stephan & Chenoweth 2008, verified). Lit Beta(2,8); Jev ~0.45

q_C.source: F3: P(systematic defection) under collective-punishment orders (Mau Mau, Herero, Guatemala: mostly out-group or stacked units)

q_X.source: F3: P(systematic defection) under orders to kill or starve the general majority population (forces' own kin among the targets; Khmer Rouge peak ~22-25% via class split). Lit and Jev (~0.55) agree

m_stack_pers.source: F3: defection multiplier for personalist regimes (coup-proofing, ethnic stacking: Makara 2013, Lee 2015; Syria 2011-13)

m_stack_olig.source: F3: same, oligarchic/party regimes (Egypt 2011 army as institution)

d_def.source: F3: share of HUMAN coercive units lost in a systematic breakdown

c_req.source: F3: share of coercive capacity an order needs; it fails if d_def x human share > 1 - c_req. A4: once automated systems carry the order the executor check is gone (a threshold, not a slow fade)

p_oust.source: F3: P(leader/faction ousted after a failed X or C order; policy resets to status quo)

OR_def.source: F3: insurgent success odds multiplier from systematic defection (Stephan & Chenoweth 2008: defections more than quadruple success, verified). Replaces def_mult

C_oust.source: F3: members' anticipated cost of ouster, output-share equivalent, weighted by P(order fails)

m0.source: cost of decent provision / output in 2026 terms

c_R.source: rentier cost relative to serve (full provision, no political rights)

w_R.source: public welfare under rentier rule relative to serve (Gulf citizens: rich, no vote)

thk_R.source: residual revolt threat under rentier rule relative to warehouse (Saudi 2011 buy-off worked; Bahrain excluded group revolted)

tau0.source: expected loss from an aggrieved population / output per yr with human security

E0.source: legitimacy + international pressure / output at full rival leverage

intl.source: extra international response (sanctions, war risk) to executing depopulation, multiple of E0 term

v0.source: F4: land/resource value freed by removing population, share of output (urban land value depends on population; settler-colonial land: Wolfe 2006, Natives Land Acts 1913/1936, US Indian removal)

v1.source: Ricardian scarcity rent as the terrestrial ceiling binds (50% mass at zero)

phi_stigma.source: recurring share of killing's moral/legitimacy cost

s_sw.source: one-time cost of switching provisioning regime, output-years (0.07-0.9; round 1 used 0.1, which with no confirmation step let blocs ratchet into harsh options)

p_exec.source: P(an ordered depopulation is carried out, operationally), EXCLUDING security-force defection, which is now explicit (F3). Round 2 U(0.7,0.95); Jev grid refusal at zero human security 0.08-0.15 -> 0.85-0.92; mixture. Failure leaves 1-5% dead and a desperate insurgency

x_thr.source: threat multiplier during execution (a population facing extermination resists harder than a warehoused one, but targeted populations historically rarely mounted effective resistance)

p_small.source: P(once security and admin are automated, the deciding circle shrinks to 1-7 people) per consolidated autocracy; otherwise >=21 (selectorate data; Jev assumes ~500)

lag_dec0.source: years from closure to strategic decision at 2026 decision speed

spd_max.source: strategic decision-speed compression at full AI R&D automation (r8d)

Tn.source: years of neglect to 10% population loss (Irish famine 12% in ~5 y)

lagX.source: years from executed depopulation decision to 10% loss

a_vote.source: welfare weight added per unit of D_dem

k_inst.source: moral/legitimacy cost multiplier per unit of D_dem

griev_trend.source: initial yearly rise of anti-AI grievance attitudes (Pew 31%->39% 'more harm' in one year). F7: logistic toward g_max instead of a hard cap at 0.55

g_max.source: F7: ceiling of the grievance-attitude share. Public-opinion saturation: Gallup US Congress disapproval peaked ~85-90% (approval 9%, Nov 2013) [M]

att_max.source: F7: ceiling of attitudinal support for political violence (replaces the 0.5 cap). Upper range in populations in open conflict: PCPSR polls, support for armed struggle ~50-60% [M]

cr_hl.source: F8: half-life (y) of a crisis provision response once grievance stops rising (CARES Act 2020 large but temporary)

s_nino.source: A7: ecological-stress index during the record 2026-27 El Nino, until mid-2028 (NOAA CPC 10 Sep 2026: Nino-3.4 +1.8 C, 75% chance of a historic event)

k_intl.source: A7: yearly decay of international pressure E0 (US withdrawal from 66 international organizations, Jan 2026; UNGA-81 walkouts; 'breakdown' not verified)

r_ab.source: share of displaced labor reabsorbed into new human work at 2026 breadth

pg_red.source: fraction of grievance removed by full provision (status loss persists): 0.1-0.6

pr_red.source: fraction of revolt hazard removed by full provision. r9c (Saudi 2011 buy-off) U(0.3,0.7), weight 0.6; Jev grid U(0.05,0.4) (almost no provision effect), weight 0.4. Reported as a disagreement

k_buy.source: autocratic buy-off of grievance while coercion still needs humans (Saudi 2011)

h_beh0.source: behavioral hostile faction share (would join sabotage/violence), 2026

att_trend.source: yearly rise of attitudinal support for political violence (PRRI 15%->23% 2021-23)

e_att.source: elasticity of behavioral hostility to attitudinal support (attitudes rose without proportional organized violence)

e_g.source: elasticity of hostility to the grievance state Gv

mdisp.source: hostile-share multiplier per 10 pp displaced (Swing riots; GTI)

Hmax.source: round-2 saturation of relative hostility; used only in the caps_v4 variant

Habs.source: F7: saturation of the BEHAVIORAL hostile share (would join sabotage/violence), absolute share of adults. Replaces the relative Hmax 5-10 and the 50%-displacement cap. Active participation in the largest revolutions/insurgencies ~3.5-15% of the population (Chenoweth 3.5% rule; mass-mobilization peaks) [M]

p_svr_hi.source: P(sustained violent resistance over ~10 y | 30% displaced, provision 0.2, high-capacity state). r9c U(0.15,0.5) weight 0.6; Jev grid U(0.12,0.35) weight 0.4

lam0_hi.source: 2026 hazard of a NEW sustained insurgency at zero displacement, high-capacity bloc (UCDP onset 0.1-0.5%/yr for high-capacity states; none in US/China for decades)

lam0_weak.source: same, low-capacity bloc of 2-3B people (new campaigns beyond the 2026 baseline)

elec.source: revolt risk diverted to elections per unit D_dem

aU.source: anocracy excess onset risk (inverted U, Hegre et al. 2001)

d_surv.source: onset hazard factor at fully automated security/surveillance (Xu 2021 digital repression; Xinjiang)

rd.source: P(consistent high-capacity repression suppresses sustained resistance within 5 y)

k_auto.source: extra suppression effectiveness of automated security

def_mult.source: insurgent success odds multiplier when security fully automated

p_dem_suc.source: P(a successful violent campaign leads to democracy; otherwise a new narrow autocracy) (Chenoweth-Stephan)

k_bf.source: backfire from repression that fails to deter; also added after collective punishment

dfd.source: hostility damping after a defeated revolt (decays over 5 y)

ins_mort.source: crackdown/insurgency deaths per year of active insurgency, fraction of population

p_lcp.source: P(lethal collective punishment during an insurgency | labor unneeded, weak external check)

f_lcp.source: share of the aggrieved regional population killed per episode (Mau Mau ~1-2% of Kikuyu, Gaza ~3%, Herero 65-80%)

m_d.source: excess mortality/yr of status-stripped, welfare-dependent displaced adults (deaths of despair ~0.2-0.3%/yr in the affected group; Native American life-expectancy gap ~0.3-0.5%/yr)

hgain.source: offset of despair mortality by AI-era health gains at full automation

tau_sab.source: sabotage cost to automated infrastructure / output per yr at reference hostility

host_ins.source: F4: coalition hostility added by active insurgency (insurgent threat radicalizes elites toward eliminationist policy: Valentino, Huth & Balch-Lindsay 2004; Harff 2003; Straus 2006; Kteily et al. 2016)

host_H.source: coalition hostility added by public hostility; F7: smooth saturation host_H*(1-exp(-(Hr-1)/3)) instead of a cap at 4x

h_on.source: autocratization onset hazard per democracy-year, all countries (V-Dem: 10 new of 179)

h_bd.source: breakdown hazard of a rich democracy at intact leverage (Przeworski et al. 2000)

M_lev.source: erosion hazard multiplier as leverage goes 1 -> 0

e_rate.source: LDI decline per year during an episode (US -0.218 since 2023)

p_uturn.source: P(episode reverses before breakdown | leverage intact)

em_jump.source: D_dem drop from emergency powers at war/insurgency onset

c_max.source: cap on conflict-intensity index relative to 2026

w_pair.source: US-China war hazard per year at 2026 intensity

w_row.source: major-war hazard per year for a non-US/China bloc at 2026 intensity (x0.5 Europe, x1 Russia_MENA, x0.8 South Asia, x0.6 Global South)

ukr_rem.source: remaining years of the Russia-Ukraine war from Oct 2026

w_mort.source: war deaths per war-year as a fraction of a whole bloc's population (Ukraine ~1%/yr for the belligerent; blocs are larger)

p_nuc.source: P(nuclear use | a major war of a nuclear-armed bloc)

f_nuc.source: bloc population share killed if nuclear weapons are used

m_war.source: moral cost of killing in war/insurgency vs peacetime

mc_ai.source: moral-cost factor at fully AI-mediated targeting

eco_mult.source: conflict multiplier at severe ecological stress (1.2-4)

eco_land.source: rise in land/resource value share at severe ecological stress (50% mass at zero)

p_id.source: P(depopulation/successionist ideology taken up by a closed bloc's rulers within 9 y, no war; war x2.5). Calibrated so P(US or China bloc by 2045) ~0.08 (r9d)

id_hl.source: half-life of a ruling ideology (regime turnover, generational change), years

id_share.source: coalition hostility share added when that ideology is fully held (builds over ~4 y)

T_full.source: A8: years for an executed depopulation carried by automated force plus economic strangulation to reach >=99.9% loss if unconstrained (hazard ramps linearly from the lagX rate); no precedent at this scale, so wide (A10)

dL_means.source: A8: horizon doublings beyond M3 (90% software capability) at which a means of rapid mass killing is available to a closed bloc's coalition (abstract availability; probit width 1 doubling)

h_use.source: A8/A9: yearly hazard that a coalition executing depopulation uses such a means once available

f_eng.source: A8: share of the remaining targeted population killed by one use (abstract)

p_tot0.source: A11: P(the designation targets near-total removal from the start); otherwise an initial partial target f0

f0.source: A11: initial partial target (share of population) when the designation is partial

k_esc.source: A11: yearly hazard of escalating a partial designation to near-total, per unit of perceived revenge threat (grievance/0.5 x (1 + active insurgency)): any free surviving community is a seed that can organize and take revenge (dark-forest logic)

rem.source: A11: captive remnant kept without rights (scenario: ~8 million of 8 billion = 0.1%)

k_col.source: A9: yearly hazard of tacit collusion (economic or hot war on each other's populations) between two coalitions that both execute depopulation, when incentives favor it

b_col.source: A9: rulers' value of collusion (cover, elimination of the other bloc's human seed), relative units

c_self.source: A9: rulers' value of their own survival in the same units; collude iff b_col > (1 - s_bunk) x p_nx x c_self

s_bunk.source: A9: rulers' own survival probability in a nuclear exchange given bunker preparations

p_nx.source: A9: P(a collusive war goes nuclear)

f_nx.source: A9: share of each colluding bloc's remaining population killed by a nuclear exchange

w_col.source: A9: yearly deaths of the remaining population from collusive economic/hot war (on top of the executing bloc's own means)

sel_top.source: B1: moral-cost AND refusal multiplier for the person at the top of an autocratic coalition (selection: those who fight their way to that much power have less of the brake). Members of an autocratic coalition get sel_top^0.5. Anchors (qualitative, mapped by judgment): psychopathy ~1% general population vs ~3-4% in senior corporate roles (Babiak & Hare 2007; Babiak, Neumann & Hare 2010); elevated fearless dominance among US presidents (Lilienfeld et al. 2012, JPSP 103:489); tyrants as malignant narcissists with superego deficits (Glad 2002, Pol. Psych.); revealed casualty tolerance: Russia ~1.1-1.25M casualties incl. ~250-500k killed by early/mid 2026 (UK DI Oct 2025 1.118M; Telegraph Feb 2026 >1.25M; BBC/GCHQ May 2026 ~500k killed) for territorial aims; DPRK camps 80-120k prisoners, 'hundreds of thousands' dead over five decades (UN COI 2014); Great Purge 681,692 executions 1937-38, 3 of 5 marshals; Great Leap famine continued ~3 y

id_mor.source: B1: share of the remaining moral cost removed when a depopulation ideology is fully held (reframing as kindness / ecological reset: moral justification and euphemistic labelling, Bandura 1999)

k_prg.source: B2: yearly purge hazard per coalition member at full incentive (leader holds all force, needs no human staff). Anchors: 70% of the 1934 CC arrested by 1939 (~0.24/yr); Great Purge removed 3 of 5 marshals and ~13 of 15 army commanders; Saddam 1979; Turkey post-2016

prg_c0.source: B2: share of the purge incentive present even while the leader still needs competent human staff (loyalty-competence trade-off, Egorov & Sonin 2011; purges happened in fully human regimes). The rest scales with (1 - human share of security/admin)

c_cc.source: B2: P(counter-coup) per purge event, times the rest of the coalition's share of force (1 - S_L). Svolik 2012: insiders remove ~2/3 of ousted autocrats; Sudduth 2017: dictators purge when elites' capacity to oust them is temporarily low

k_par.source: B2/B4: purge-incentive multiplier per 10% of the population already killed deliberately (scenario: 'guilt turns to paranoia'; fear of retribution after atrocities)

k_extp.source: B2: reduction of purge incentive when a rival of comparable automated force exists (Goldring: purges more likely when foreign and revolutionary threats are low)

k_am.source: B3/B5: force multiplier of automated over human-staffed forces at equal output (Ukraine: drones cause ~60-80% of front-line casualties, r9a [K]; colonial tech asymmetry, e.g. Omdurman 1898 [M]). Kinetic power M = output x (1 + k_am x automated share of security)

k_ret.source: B4: multiplier on the rulers' perceived threat from survivors per 10% of population already killed deliberately (also scales A11 escalation). Archigos: most leaders removed irregularly are exiled, jailed or killed (research/m5)

k_xb.source: B5: yearly hazard that an executing closed coalition extends depopulation to a bloc it can overpower, when its payoff test passes

dom_thr.source: B5: share of combined kinetic power (aggressor / (aggressor + target)) the aggressor needs before attacking

p_ret0.source: B5: P(a nuclear-armed target retaliates) at parity; falls as (1 - dominance) since an overwhelmingly dominant automated force can suppress a deterrent (counterforce, defence). Arsenals: FAS 2026 (US 3,700, Russia 4,400, China 620, France 290, UK 225, India 190, Pakistan 170, Israel 90, DPRK 60)

k_rep.source: B5: yearly hazard of repelling a cross-bloc campaign, times the target's share of combined kinetic power

cn_ppp.source: B3/B5: multiplier on China's military-expenditure share for purchasing-power parity (market-rate SIPRI figure understates Chinese military output)

k_kit.source: B6/F6: draw of fixed automation kit on the shared robot-input budget (magnets, chips, actuators) per worker-equivalent, relative to a general-purpose robot
